keySentence: The jungle has its own law.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Mowgli was a boy who lived deep in the Indian jungle. Wolves had raised him and a bear named Baloo had taught him. The jungle was not a wild and lawless place at all. Every animal knew what was right and what was wrong. Strong animals could not just take from weak ones whenever they wanted. There were rules about hunting and about the water hole. The jungle has its own law.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Mowgli was a boy who had grown up deep inside the Indian jungle. He had been raised by wolves and taught by a bear named Baloo. The jungle was not a wild and lawless place the way outsiders imagined. Every animal knew exactly what was allowed and what was forbidden by all. The strong did not simply take from the weak whenever they felt like it. There were rules about hunting and about water and about how animals greeted each other. Mowgli had learned these rules before he had learned almost anything else at all. The jungle has its own law.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: To a stranger the Indian jungle might look like a place of complete and terrifying chaos. But Mowgli had grown up inside it and he understood that this appearance was entirely deceiving. The wolves had raised him, and the bear Baloo had patiently taught him the rules from a very young age. Every creature from the smallest jackal to the largest elephant lived within a framework of shared expectations. There were rules about hunting, about the waterhole, about how to greet another species, about when to strike and when to walk away. These were not written anywhere — they were carried in the memory of every animal and enforced by the whole jungle together. Mowgli had learned them before he had learned almost anything else about what it meant to be alive in that place. The jungle, he came to see, was not the absence of civilization — it was simply a different kind of it entirely. The jungle has its own law.
